content.title: Miami Heat vs Philadelphia 76ers Live Stream: How to Watch NBA
content.text: The Philadelphia 76ers look to maintain their lead over the Miami Heat in the Eastern Conference standings at home on Thursday. The Miami Heat look to take a 2-0 season series lead against the Philadelphia 76ers on Thursday night. The Heat are going for their fourth win in five games, and trying to bounce back from a loss on Tuesday against the Milwaukee Bucks that ended a three-game winning streak. The Sixers have to be feeling great right now since Joel Embiid returned to the lineup in their last game against the Indiana Pacers after missing five games with a knee and shin injury. The 76ers will go for their third win in a row today. That comes after Philadelphia lost four in a row and five of its previous six. The Sixers sit in the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference standings, and Miami has a great opportunity to close the gap, sitting just 1.5 games behind Philadelphia for the eighth seed. Miami won in Philly back on Nov. 23 in Game 1, 127-117, with Norman Powell going off for a game-high 32 points, while Kel’el Ware added 20 points and put up 16 rebounds. It was the Heat’s fourth straight victory. Tyrese Maxey scored 27 points to lead Philadelphia, but even then, the Sixers missed Embiid for the seventh straight game with that nagging right knee injury. Philadelphia is just the 1.5-point favorite to defend home court tonight, with Embiid listed as a game-time decision. The 76ers are coming off a dominating 135-114 victory over the East’s worst Indiana Pacers on Tuesday. The Sixers won the series 3-0 with the finale coming in April. Tyrese Maxey played great once again, scoring a game-high 32 points, and he nearly put up a triple-double by leading Philadelphia with nine rebounds and eight assists. Embiid looked like he didn’t miss any time at all in his return, scoring another 27 points. Indiana got out to a decent first-quarter lead, but Philadelphia didn’t let the Pacers creep back in the game the rest of the way. The 76ers were on fire from the field, shooting 58 percent. Miami is coming off a 128-117 loss to the Bucks on Tuesday. The Bucks jumped ahead with a season-high 32 points from Kevin Porter Jr., and Bobby Portis, along with Ryan Rollins, both scored 21 points apiece. It was enough to overshadow a team-high 26 points from Miami’s Powell. It was Milwaukee’s fourth win in its last five games, and the Heat couldn’t take advantage of Giannis Antetokounmpo missing his 12th game in a row. Bam Adebayo put up another 18 points with nine rebounds. It was a tough loss for the Heat since they led by nine in the fourth quarter.
